frozen_claims.text: yad etad bahudhā proktam āṇavaṃ śivatāptaye — this āṇava, taught manifoldly, aims at Śiva-hood: the lowest rung is already teleologically complete.
tatrāntar antarāviśya — entering into the intervals therein: the practice is penetration between (antar-antara) the manifold forms, not piling more on.
viśrāmyet savidhe pade — rest in the proximate station: the optative commands settling, and savidha carries both nearness and kindredness — the resting place is already of the goal's kind.
The āṇava rung: multiply taught, it works by entering the gaps between its own forms and resting in the near-kindred station — ascent by deepening, not by adding.
tato 'py āṇava-saṃtyāgāt śāktīṃ bhūmim upāśrayet — by abandoning even the āṇava: each rung is climbed by leaving it (api concedes even this lowest hold).
tato 'pi śāmbhavīm evam — then likewise the Śāmbhava: the same abandon-and-resort motion repeats upward.
tāratamya-kramāt sphuṭam — in graded sequence, distinctly: the rungs stay distinct (sphuṭam), no blurring of means.
The ladder law: resort by abandonment, rung by rung, each distinct — the mechanism that makes the final means-lessness (v3) a completion rather than a refusal.

kramodita-vibodha-mahāmarīci-saṃpūrita-prasara-bhairava-bhāva-bhāgī — partaking of the Bhairava-state whose expanse is filled with the great rays of sequentially-arisen awakening: the climbed ladder's fruit in one compound.
ante 'bhyupāya-nirapekṣatayā eva — in the end with utter independence from means: the anupāya moment (Tantrasara 1 caturvidham; TAL ch2 gatopāya).
nityaṃ svātmānam āviśati garbhitaviśvarūpam — enters forever one's own self, universe-wombed: the self entered already contains the all.
The crown: ladder-ripened awakening fills the Bhairava expanse, means fall away, and entry into one's own self is entry into the all-containing — liberation as recognition, not acquisition.
